text:
Ivar Stenberg went second overall in June, one pick after Gavin McKenna, and by late October the Sharks had him on their top line beside Macklin Celebrini. He's 19 and has 16 points in 26 games, nine on the power play, where his game lives right now. The rookie headlines say he's trending up and earning trust.

His goals are earned: eight on 7.3 expected. What's been held back is everything around him. The Sharks have scored 6.4 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, and that kind of bad luck usually swings back, which is why we had him as a point sleeper tonight. The harder part is five on five, where San Jose takes only 44% of the expected goals with him on. That's the normal price of a teenager learning North American ice. All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) finds no clear strength or weakness yet. Our range projects 41 to 65 points. His last SHL season translated to about 41.
